questions.question: Comment on the freezing point and boiling point of milk.
questions.solution_html:
•  The normal freezing point of milk is approximately \(-0.54^\circ C\).
  •  It is lower than that of pure water because milk contains dissolved substances such as
  • lactose and mineral salts.
  •  The freezing point is relatively constant in normal milk.
  •  Addition of water raises the freezing point towards \(0^\circ C\), making freezing-point
  • measurement useful for detecting possible adulteration with water.
  •  Milk boils at a temperature slightly above that of pure water at the same atmospheric
  • pressure.
  •  At normal atmospheric pressure, its boiling point is approximately \(100.1–100.2^\circ
  • C\).
  •  Dissolved solids in milk cause this slight elevation in boiling point.
  •  The boiling point decreases at lower atmospheric pressure and increases at higher
  • pressure.
  • Packaging and storage: The cheese is packed hygienically and stored under refrigeration.
  • Quality of raw milk: Initial microbial load, acidity, adulteration and the health of the milch
  • animals influence the quality of milk during transportation.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: animals influence the quality of milk during transportation.

questions.question: Describe the carbohydrate and mineral value of milk.
questions.solution_html:
•  Lactose is the principal carbohydrate in milk.
  •  It is generally present at about 4.5–5.0%.
  •  Lactose provides energy and contributes to the mild sweetness of milk.
  •  It promotes calcium absorption and serves as a substrate for lactic acid bacteria during
  • fermentation.
  •  Fermentation of lactose produces lactic acid, which is important in the manufacture of
  • curd, yoghurt and cheese.
  •  Milk is a good source of calcium and phosphorus, which are essential for the
  • development and maintenance of bones and teeth.
  •  Potassium helps maintain fluid balance and supports normal muscle and nerve function.
  •  Sodium and chloride help maintain electrolyte balance.
  •  Magnesium supports normal enzyme and muscle functions.
  •  Milk also contains small amounts of trace minerals, including zinc, iron and copper.
  • Availability of trained personnel: Properly trained milk handlers and drivers help maintain
  • hygiene, temperature control and accurate records.
  • Measures to improve transportation
  •  Cool milk promptly after milking.
  •  Use clean, food-grade milk cans and properly sanitized tankers.
  •  Maintain the cold chain and minimize transportation delays.
  •  Establish efficient collection centres and bulk milk cooling facilities.
  •  Conduct regular quality testing at collection and reception points.
  • Conclusion: Efficient transportation requires proper cooling, hygienic handling, suitable
  • infrastructure and effective milk collection systems. These measures help preserve milk quality
  • from the farm to the dairy plant.

questions.question: Describe the manufacturing process of Yoghurt. Explain with the help of a flow diagram.
questions.solution_html:

  • milk. The characteristic flavour and texture develop through acid production and changes in milk
  • proteins.
  • Starter cultures
  • The traditional yoghurt starter consists of
  •  Streptococcus thermophilus
  •  Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus
  • These organisms act symbiotically and convert lactose into lactic acid.
  • Selection and filtration of milk
  • Standardization of fat and solids
  • Homogenization
  • Heat treatment (e.g. 85°C for 30 min or an equivalent validated treatment)
  • Cooling to inoculation temperature (usually 42–45°C)
  • Addition of yoghurt starter culture
  • Incubation and fermentation
  • Cooling
  • Packaging (for stirred yoghurt, stirring and filling are performed as appropriate)
  • Refrigerated storage and distribution
